findings.text: follow-on: the manifest's baseline_suite failure_ids names tests/test_crew_obligations_reads_scoring_without_observing_or_dispatching.py, which does not exist; the base log's summary line names tests/test_crew_obligations.py::test_obligations_reads_scoring_without_observing_or_dispatching, so a consumer that computes the added set with ledger.added_failure_ids over the JSON fields reads one spurious added failure where the log-derived count is 0.

follow-on: the manifest's negative_control_log (repro-parity-divergence.log) exercises the mixed-state parity case, not the declared mutation (restore the whole-ledger load; the never-called case fails), which is the run recorded in gate-negative-control.log, so the declared string and the named log describe two different mutations.

follow-on: the fast path admits a per-run file only when the node token in its run id equals the worktree directory name (_run_id_names_node at obligations.py:228), so a record whose node id differs from its retained tree's directory name is reached only by the whole-ledger fallback, and a tree that another record also names can resolve in the fast path to a different run than the merged reader would pick; the five generated mixed states do not cover this shape.

item_verdicts.diff: read the range below commit by commit; eight commits, three files. The production change is one file, reckon/crew/obligations.py, which adds _run_id_names_node, _run_file_record, _names_worktree, _aggregate_rows, _ledger_order_key and _holding_record and rewrites the matching loop in _held_worktrees (obligations.py:408-437).
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py with a parity case, a never-called case (ledger.runs and ledger.load patched to raise) and a fallback case, plus a base-arm and head-arm gate; the manifest records gate-base.log 2 failed 54 passed EXIT=1 and gate-head.log 1 failed 55 passed EXIT=1, and added_failures_from_gate_logs over those two logs returns count 0 with no ids, so the head arm adds none.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that obligations._held_worktrees stops loading crew.json whole and resolves each inspected tree from the per-run ledger file of the run that named it; reckon/crew/obligations.py:370 _held_worktrees now reads ledger._run_files at obligations.py:412 and resolves each tree through _holding_record at obligations.py:330 over both the aggregate rows and the per-run files, keeping the whole-ledger read only as a fallback for a tree neither source names.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the run-dir manifest; it records the two gate arms with revisions and exits, the negative control, the timing arms (base 3.324 s, head first call 1.198 s), and the aggregate-row source under evidence_inputs, but its baseline_suite failure id names a module file that does not exist (tests/test_crew_obligations_reads_scoring_without_observing_or_dispatching.py) where the base log names tests/test_crew_obligations.py::test_obligations_reads_scoring_without_observing_or_dispatching.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declares reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py, docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/held-worktrees-read-run-files.html and a figures directory; a diff of the reviewed range touches exactly those three files (17 deleted, 625 inserted), and the figures directory is never created.

justifications.durability: tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py:327 test_inspected_runs_are_read_from_their_own_files is red at base (gate-base.log) where the whole-ledger reader raises, and test_a_mixed_state_goes_to_the_run at :296 is red when the answering change is reverted (repro-parity-divergence.log fails file-and-aggregate-row), and each parity expectation is computed by the independent _whole_ledger_held helper at :139 rather than from the value under test.
justifications.evidence: gate-base.log and gate-head.log each open with their revision and command and end 2 failed 54 passed / 1 failed 55 passed with a bare EXIT=1 line, and added_failures_from_gate_logs over them returns count 0 with no ids, but the timing arms were measured on session s21-1c whose worktree set is empty, so they exercise only the crew.json memo and never the per-run or fallback path.
justifications.fit: the helpers in reckon/crew/obligations.py:225-368 name a mechanism (_run_id_names_node, _aggregate_rows, _ledger_order_key) with no plan, sprint or version label, matching the surrounding module; the change reaches private ledger helpers (_load_aggregate at ledger.py:670, _run_files at ledger.py:666), which is a light coupling the module did not have before.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligations.py:412 reads ledger._run_files and obligations.py:330 _holding_record resolves each inspected tree from a per-run file or an aggregate row, so the per-run read lands; but crew.json is still parsed whole by obligations.py:293 _aggregate_rows and the derivation keeps its own _AGGREGATE_ROWS index at obligations.py:288, which are the two things the plan's item 3 (falls back to crew.json only for runs that do not, and builds no index of its own) says must not happen.
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed range touches only the three declared non-figure paths under reckon/crew/obligations.py, tests/test_held_worktrees_read_run_files.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/held-worktrees-read-run-files.html, and no path in it lies outside the declared scope.

manifest_note: the reviewed manifest armed baseline_suite and after_suite; the added-failure count and ids were derived from those two gate logs by this reviewer via reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs, which reads the log text rather than the reviewed manifest's failure_ids field; the reviewed run's head gate arm ran at cd1dffd658d47119c7e0ced0d273d128a3016921 while the reviewed head is 93c328388e38b22384aaf86bfef63eede4808581, whose remaining delta is docs/evidence commits only.
